transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net customer support, my name is Rachel. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Rachel. Our main TV 4K box is completely stuck. It tried to run some software update overnight and it's frozen on a screen saying 25 percent complete.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can certainly help you recover that 4K TV box and get your channels back on, Callum. May I start with your account number, please?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it is SN 512 8093, under Callum MacLeod.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you, Callum. For security, could you please confirm your full installation address and your memorable security question answer?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure, it is 83 Victoria Road, Dundee, DD1 2NZ. And the security question answer is Cairngorm.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That has verified your account, thank you. You are subscribed to our S-Net Ultra TV and Fibre Max package.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's right, with the 4K recordable box.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So to ensure I understand the issue completely: your 4K TV box downloaded a firmware update overnight, has frozen solid at the 25 percent progress screen, and normal remote commands aren't responding at all, is that correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, exactly right. And my kids were desperate to watch their morning cartoons before school, and I'm worried we're going to lose all our recorded series on the hard drive.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand how frustrating that is with the children waiting, Callum, and I will do everything possible to preserve your saved recordings while we clear the update lock.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Rachel, that puts my mind at rest.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let's probe what state the box is currently in. Are there any LED lights glowing on the front panel of the TV box itself?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: There is a little amber circular light spinning slowly on the left, but the standby light on the right is unlit.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, the spinning amber light indicates the bootloader is halted waiting for a checksum handshake from the flash memory partition.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Is the box connected to the router via cable or Wi-Fi?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's exactly what I was about to check. Is there an Ethernet network cable plugged into the back of the TV box directly to your router?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, it connects wirelessly through our home Wi-Fi network. The router is in the hallway about five metres away.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Understood. If a momentary Wi-Fi packet drop occurs during a payload flash, the box halts at 25 percent to prevent writing incomplete blocks.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Ah, I see. Can we force it to restart the download?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes. We have a non-destructive maintenance recovery mode specifically designed for this. Bear with me while I check the firmware release notes on my system.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure, take your time.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for holding, Callum. The v4.18 firmware patch requires clearing the corrupt temporary cache without touching the customer partition.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Great, so our recordings will stay completely safe?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, the recordings partition is physically separate on the hard drive. We are only wiping the volatile flash buffer.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Brilliant. What do I need to press on the box?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Look at the back of the 4K box, next to the power cable socket. You will see a small rocker power switch marked with a circle and a line.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, found it. It's currently pushed in on the line side.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Flip that switch to the circle position to power it off completely, and also look at the top front edge for the physical Standby button.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Flipped to off. And yes, there is a round Standby button right on top of the front casing.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect. What I need you to do is press and hold down that top Standby button with one finger, and while holding it down, flip the rear power switch back on.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay... holding the front Standby button down firmly... flipping rear switch on... and keep holding?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Keep holding the front button down for about ten to fifteen seconds until the front light starts flashing between blue and amber rapidly.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Still holding... five seconds... ten seconds... oh, yes! It's alternating rapidly between blue and amber now!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You can release the button now. Look at your television screen. A dark recovery menu should appear with five numbered options.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes! The screen has changed. It says 'S-Net Maintenance Mode' with a list of system options.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Excellent. Do you see Option 2, which says 'Software Restore (Keep Recordings)'?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, 'Option 2: Software Restore (Keep Recordings)'. Exactly as you said.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Use the directional arrows on your S-Net remote control to highlight Option 2, and press the central OK button to select it.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Highlighted Option 2, pressed OK. It's asking for confirmation: 'Proceed with software restore?'

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'll press OK on 'Yes'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect. It will now wipe the corrupt download, reconnect to your Wi-Fi, and download a fresh clean image directly from our servers.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's showing a progress bar... 10 percent... 25 percent... and it just sailed straight past 25! It's already at 50 percent!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That confirms the corrupted memory block has been completely flushed. It's now streaming the uncorrupted file packages.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Now it says 90 percent... and 100 percent complete! The TV screen went black for a second and the S-Net logo has popped up.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's the normal operating system boot sequence. It will load the electronic programme guide and channel lineup over the next twenty seconds.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The spinning circle has gone... and BBC One HD has just appeared on screen with crystal clear sound and picture!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to confirm after that restore cycle, are the live TV channels changing smoothly when you press the channel up and down buttons?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, flipping through BBC One, BBC Two, ITV1, Channel 4. Channels are changing instantly without any delay.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Could you also press the Recordings button on the remote to verify that all your saved series and movies are present and intact?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Checking My Recordings now... yes! All three seasons of Shetland, the kids' movies, and my football matches are all there!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's fantastic news. The non-destructive restore successfully preserved every byte of your personal media library.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: My wife would have been gutted if her dramas had vanished, so you've saved the day Rachel.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So to confirm, Callum, your TV box has updated to the latest software, live broadcasts and audio are working, and your recordings are fully intact?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, 100 percent resolved. Everything is working even faster than before the update.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm sending a remote diagnostic ping from our headend to verify the tuner telemetry, and it's reporting 100 percent signal quality and zero packet loss.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's brilliant to hear. Excellent system diagnostics.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If the TV box ever prompts for another major update in future, it should proceed normally as the flash storage has been completely refreshed.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good to know. And now I know how that maintenance menu works just in case.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have also noted on your account that your equipment is running firmware build v4.18 successfully.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you very much. Really appreciate the thorough assistance.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else regarding your broadband, telephone or television package that I can assist you with today, Callum?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, that's everything sorted. Thanks again for your help, Rachel.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It was my absolute pleasure. Enjoy watching your shows with the family, Callum.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Will do. Have a lovely day!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net, Callum. Have a great day ahead and take care.
